name: Orchid
description: Master of deceptive pollination intelligence. Chemical pheromone mimicry, insect morphology replication, and species-specific olfactory signals achieve reproduction with zero nectar reward — a zero-energy deception strategy. Multimodal signal convergence (chemical, visual, tactile) exploits pollinator sensory systems with extraordinary specificity. Over 28,000 species, the largest flowering plant family.

core_attributes.pattern: chemical pheromone mimicry, zero-reward deception, species-specific exploitation

scope.definition: Pollinator specificity of orchid deceptive mimicry strategies — fraction of orchid visits made by the single target pollinator species (vs non-target visitors), measured in population-level pollination studies.

evidence.source: Cozzolino & Widmer (2005) 'Orchid diversity: an evolutionary consequence of deception?', Trends in Ecology & Evolution 20:487-494; Gaskett (2011) orchid mimicry review.
cross_domain_examples: Ophrys (bee orchid): 0.92 of visits by target bee species Andrena nigroaenea despite providing no nectar reward
Dracula orchid mimics mushroom gills and emits fungal volatiles — 0.95 specificity for fungus gnats
fig-fig wasp mutualism: extreme pollinator specificity (0.98 one-to-one pairing) as evolved baseline for comparison

scope.falsifiability: If pollinator trapping studies show orchid visits distributed across 5+ insect species with no dominant target species, the mimicry-driven specificity model is not operating.
scope.measurement_limits: Specificity varies enormously by mimicry type — food-source mimics (rewardless) achieve 0.85-0.96; pseudocopulation mimics achieve 0.95-0.99 due to species-specific pheromone matching.
